# partiteai_user_metric (Resource)

A metric of your own for a model to judge a conversation against. Put one in a rubric to have it scored. Requires an enterprise deployment.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `complexity` (String) Model complexity to judge at. One of `LOW`, `MEDIUM` or `HIGH`.
- `name` (String) Resource name
- `prompt` (String) What the judging model is asked.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Resource description
- `examples` (Attributes List) Worked examples shown to the judging model, to anchor its scoring. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--examples))
- `input_fields` (Attributes List) Values a rubric supplies when it uses this metric. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--input_fields))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the resource was created
- `id` (String) Resource identifier
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the resource was last updated

<a id="nestedatt--examples"></a>
### Nested Schema for `examples`

Required:

- `judgment` (String) Why that scenario earns that rating.
- `rating` (Number) Score this example earns.
- `scenario` (String) What happened, as the judge would see it.


<a id="nestedatt--input_fields"></a>
### Nested Schema for `input_fields`

Required:

- `description` (String) What the value is for.
- `label` (String) Name shown to a person filling it in.
- `name` (String) Key a rubric supplies this value under.
- `required` (Boolean) Whether a rubric has to supply it.
- `type` (String) One of `STRING`, `NUMBER`, `BOOLEAN`, `STRING_LIST` or `JSON_OBJECT`.
